question: A 29-year-old woman, gravida 1, para 1, comes to the physician for the evaluation of a painful mass in her left breast for several days. She has no fevers or chills. She has not noticed any changes in the right breast. She has no history of serious illness. Her last menstrual period was 3 weeks ago. She appears anxious. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 80/min, respirations are 13/min, and blood pressure is 130/75 mm Hg. Examination shows a palpable, mobile, tender mass in the left upper quadrant of the breast. Ultrasound shows a 1.75-cm, well-circumscribed anechoic mass with posterior acoustic enhancement. The patient says that she is very concerned that she may have breast cancer and wishes further diagnostic testing. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management of this patient?

options.opc: MRI scan of the left breast

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Palpable, mobile, tender mass in the left upper quadrant of the breast" -> "1.75-cm, well-circumscribed anechoic mass with posterior acoustic enhancement on ultrasound" -> "Possible benign breast lesion" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The patient presents with a palpable, mobile, tender mass in the left upper quadrant of the breast, which on ultrasound appears as a 1.75-cm, well-circumscribed anechoic mass with posterior acoustic enhancement, suggestive of a possible benign breast lesion. Given this presentation, the most appropriate next step in management would be a core needle biopsy to further evaluate the nature of the mass and guide treatment decisions.
analysis: The patient's presentation with a palpable, mobile, tender mass in the left breast, along with the ultrasound findings of a well-circumscribed anechoic mass with posterior acoustic enhancement, suggests a possible benign breast lesion. Given this scenario, the most appropriate next step in management would be a core needle biopsy to obtain tissue samples for further evaluation and to guide treatment decisions. This approach aligns with standard medical practice for evaluating breast masses.
